Atom order is conserved in all blocks, so H9 is the alcohol hydrogen, O5 is the ether oxygen and O8 is the alcohol oxygen. Intramolecular O-H···O hydrogen bonding to the ether oxygen is the dominant stabiliser and is assessed from the H9···O5 distance. O-H···O geometrical screening was done first: H9···O5 ≈ 2.20–2.35 Å is a good H-bond, ≈ 2.7–3.0 Å is a weak/strained interaction, >≈3.1 Å is essentially no H-bond. The good H-bonders are therefore ranked ahead of weak/non-bonders. Within the H-bonding set the shorter H9···O5 distance is taken as a proxy for a stronger, better-linearised H-bond and for lower gauche/eclipsing strain along the C1–C4–O5–C6–C7 backbone. reason: The 23-atom XYZ blocks are the same connectivity. Mapping the atom order gives O, C1 carbonyl, C2, C3 methyl branch, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8. The Euclidean end-to-end distance of those two atoms is a cheap, reproducible proxy for overall compactness/folding: a shorter end-to-end distance implies more intramolecular contacts and, on average, less extended, less strained conformations, whereas a longer distance signals an extended, more sterically exposed arrangement. Distances were computed from the deposited coordinates for atom 1 and atom 22. Values cluster around 4.3–4.7 Å and the ordering is monotonic with the visual compactness of the structures. Several pairs are essentially numerical duplicates – 1≈21, 7≈26, 12≈25, 10≈23 and 14≈22 – with sub-0.1 Å first-atom differences, so their relative order is uncertain and they are kept adjacent. The ranking therefore follows increasing end-to-end distance, i.e. increasing apparent extension/strain, with the caveat that true relative free energies also depend on detailed torsional eclipsing, close non-bonded H…H contacts and possible O…H intramolecular hydrogen-bond geometry that cannot be fully resolved from a single static geometry. The ordering is therefore a chemically reasonable heuristic, not a quantitative energy order, and the near-degenerate duplicate groups are acknowledged as uncertain.
